messages:
Alex: Heads-up — I've been seeing sustained queueing in us-west1 GPU pools for ~6m. Token ledger shows steady drain though avg latency looked normal.
Maria: Which metric is spiking — TPM or RPM?
Alex: RPM climbing. Pool TPM alloc at 1.2k, but observed requests/sec ~180 -> ~3.6k RPM. Admission controller started queuing.
Kevin: Small chat clients firing many tiny requests; RPM-sensitive throttles get hit. :sweat_smile: 
Anya: Can you paste admission logs + token snapshot? Need batch size distro.
Alex: logs:
```
[admission] pool=us-west1-gpu-1 tokens_available=1180 tpm_limit=1200 rpm_limit=2400 inflight=96 queued=58
[request] avg_tokens=12 avg_latency_ms=45 reqs_per_min=10800
```
Maria: reqs_per_min=10800 looks like per-global, not per-pool. Check aggregation windows.
Kevin: Controller uses 1m sliding window, ledger uses 1m-smoothed TPM. Burstiness makes short spikes overflow queue though TPM steady.
Anya: Hypothesis: token accounting treats tokens as primary unit but request churn (many tiny replies) creates req-rate pressure not captured by TPM. We need request-count gating.
eng-sre-bot: Incident created: #INC-20380 — us-west1 backpressure. Pager: @Kevin @Anya
Kevin: Quick mitigation: enable rpm_gate for us-west1 for 5m to throttle request-rate separate from token bucket.
Alex: Flip done. queued dropped 58 -> 12 in ~45s. Latency stable.
Maria: Long-term options:
- add request-count budget (R-Token) so tiny responses consume both tokens and request units
- per-pool rpm_metering with dynamic safety margin when GPU util >70%
- adaptive min-charge based on median prompt length per tenant
- noisy-tenant label + auto-routing to isolated shards
Kevin: Cost/complexity sorting: rpm_metering (low), noisy-label+routing (medium), R-Token (high), adaptive min-charge (highest due to pricing complexity).
Anya: Rollout plan: start with rpm_metering + short cool-down; evaluate R-Token after signal tuning.
eng-oncall: Also saw NAT gateway conn saturation ~12% earlier — added jitter to inflight counts but not primary cause.
Maria: Ops note: rpm_gate reduced small-request churn and saved ~8% GPU cycles in burst pool — estimated $1.7k/month for current us-west1 traffic.
Kevin: If this recurs, bump regional burst capacity or move high-req tenants to Dedicated.
Anya: For the postmortem capture per-tenant rpm, avg_tokens, queue_length, admission_cpu, nat_conn_util.
Alex: Creating Grafana panel "rpm vs tpm pressure" and annotating flips.
Maria: I'll draft the short-term policy patch and open the admission-controller PR.
Kevin: ping me the PR link when up @Maria
Maria: will post in ~15m
Alex: Thanks — will check back at +1h.
